build.results:
## Question
Can a constant symplectic factorisation R = R' M (M(z) = exp(m1 z + m2 z^2 + m3 z^3) in the normalised canonical basis, colour-mixing allowed) make the polar part of each of the 7 genus-2 stable graphs of the formal quintic equal to c_Gamma t_c^-2 (leading pole untouched, subleading 1/t_c coefficient zero)?

## Answer
No, for a structural reason that the computation confirms exactly: the s^-5 coefficient (hence the t_c^-1 coefficient c'_Gamma = c_-5 + (7/5) c_Gamma) of every colour-summed stable graph is independent of M. A weight-w monomial in the m's (weight k for m_k) shifts the valuation by +4w and the exponent class mod 5 by -w, so weight 1 lives on s^-6, s^-1, s^4, ...; weight 2 on s^-2, s^3, ...; weight 3 (incl. m3) on s^2, ...; only weight 0 (the point-frame value) sits on s^-10 and s^-5. The obstruction per graph is exactly the point-frame t_c^-1 coefficient: -791/15360000, -1771/3840000, 41/12800, 743/15360000, -41/153600, 37/160000, -173/64000 (graphs 1..7; they sum to 0, the total having no 1/t_c term). The full system, version (a) (edge graphs only) and version (b) (only the 1/t_c targets) are all inconsistent, each at the single pair (Gamma, s^-5); nothing else obstructs. To move the 1/t_c coefficient of a stable graph one needs weight = 0 mod 5 (impossible at genus 2, where the total z-weight is <= 3) or a q-dependent M (not the user's constant choice; the scalar version was ruled out in SCALAR_SCAN s.5).

What CAN be done: the non-u-series polar coefficients s^-6, s^-1 (linear in m1) and s^-2 (quadratic in m1, linear in m2) are zero in the point frame and stay zero on an explicit 16-dimensional family of (m1, m2) (m3 is free and never polar). So the subleading polar coefficients of each stable graph can be "offset to zero" only in the sense of keeping them zero; the 1/t_c coefficients are frame invariants among constant symplectic factorisations.

## Implementation (new modules, no existing module changed)
- fq_sser.py: Cf applied once to the rows (gsum_q.to_sseries, alpha = beta = 0), normalised rows Q_a^{(i)} = P_a^{(i)}/Delta_i^{1/2} with Delta_i^{1/2} = zeta^{4i} x, x = Cf(C0)/L = s f0(s^5) (zeta^{3i/2} with zeta^{1/2} := zeta^3 is zeta^{4i}; checked against Cf(Delta_i)). Rows truncated at absolute O(s^24): a product with nominal valuation -10 is then exact to O(s^11) at least (worst factor Q_{2,0} has valuation +3). SympM: m1, m3 symmetric, m2 antisymmetric, M and M^-1 to z^3 with M(z)^T M(-z) = 1 asserted. Q' = Q M^-1 by z-convolution; E'_{ij}(m,n) = Sum_k (-1)^k G'_{m+1+k,n-k}; T'^{(i)}_d = (-1)^d Q'^{(i)}_{0,d-1} derived from R'^-1(z) = R'(-z)^* and eta(1, .) = eta(H^0, .); the alternative -[z^{d-1}] M(z) Q_0(-z) (R'^-1 = M R^-1) checked equal.
- fq_mvertex.py: Omega^M = M.omega by the PPZ sum over legged stable graphs (enumerated by canonical forms under S_V; |Aut| = automorphisms fixing the legs, via fq_graphs.autos_of), legs (M^-1_k)_{j i}, edges (delta - M^-1(psi) M^-1(psi')^T)/(psi+psi'), kappa-leaves -(M^-1_{e-1} 1)_j, TFT vertices Delta_j^{(2g-2+n+m)/2} WK. Key simplification used: every term is x^{2g-2+n} times an F_p constant (Sum_v (2g_v-2+n_v+m_v) = 2g-2+n+m and each leaf carries x^-1), so the vertex tensors are F_p tensors (OmegaHat) from the constant TFT Delta^hat_j^{1/2} = zeta^{4j}. Weight = psi-deficit D <= 3 (asserted), so inner graphs have <= D edges.
- fq_msum.py: outer sum per stable graph with ALL decorations with psi-deficit (fq_graphs.Decorated's Hodge pruning is not valid for M.omega, which also carries kappa and boundary classes at genus 0), summed over all colourings of half-edges and leaves as tensor contractions (graph 6: 5^6 edge-end colourings in ~1250 series products). Outer dilaton leaves are treated as extra legs of Omega^M carrying the vector T'(psi) (multilinearity), integrated over Mbar_{g_v,n_v+m_v}, exactly as gsum_q.term_value does for R.omega. One evaluation of all 7 graphs: 0.1 s.
- fq_mfit.py / fq_msolve.py / fq_mfourier.py: interpolation (161 monomials: 1, m1, m2, m3, m1 m1; 170 + 10 random symplectic M), Galois reconstruction in Q(zeta) (sigma_m(c_mu) = c_{pi_m mu}, pi_m relabelling colours i -> m i with the antisymmetry sign for m2), F_p linear algebra, Z/5 Fourier analysis; fq_mreport.py: validation blocks; genus2_symplectic.py -> logs/genus2_symplectic.log (both primes, 221 s), symplectic_result.json (all coefficients in Q(zeta), dims).

## Validation (all PASS at 2^89-1 and 2^61-1; see logs/genus2_symplectic.log)
Step 1: valuations val Q_{a,n} = -4n + (0,-1,3,2,1)_a - 1 colour-independent (n <= 4); symplecticity; E', T' at M = 1 equal the fq_rows edge/dilaton data divided by the Delta^{1/2}'s; the M = 1 graph sums reproduce pergraph_polar_out.txt (F5) for all 7 graphs through s^0, the vertex graph per colour, graph 4 at (0,0) = -31/15360000 s^-10 + 1/240000 s^-5 and at (0,1) (Q(zeta) values of the SCALAR_SCAN table), and the total through s^10.
Step 2: Omega^1 = omega; M = diag(exp(a1 zeta^-i z + a2 zeta^-3i z^3)) gives zeta^{4i(2g-2+n)} PhiVertexTable at the F4 point, the true-class point and a random point, and a non-covariant diagonal M gives the per-colour tables; symmetry; string and dilaton equations of Omega^M with 1 = Sum_k Delta_k^{-1/2} e~_k hold at a random colour-mixing M (flat unit; these test legs, edges, kappa-leaves and automorphism weights together).
Step 3: the F4 point reproduces the F4 lines of pergraph_polar_out.txt at all orders s^-10, -6, -5, -2, -1, 0 for all graphs; a random covariant diagonal point equals fq_phi.phi_frame computed through the independent N-ring route (gsum_q.genus2_sums + to_sseries) through s^10; a random non-covariant diagonal point equals fq_diag_lib.diag_frame likewise; at a random full M the TOTAL is M-independent through s^10 (decisive test), the s^-10 and s^-5 coefficients of every graph are M-independent, and s^-9, -8, -7, -4, -3 vanish.
Step 4: Vandermonde rank 161, 0 inconsistent rows, verified on 10 extra points; monomial content per graph exactly as predicted (s^-10, s^-5: constant; s^-6, s^-1: m1; s^-2: m1 m1 + m2 for graphs 1, 2, 4, 5 and m1 m1 only for 3, 6, 7; graph 1 has no s^-1 term; m3 never appears). All 604 coefficients reconstruct in Q(zeta); cross-prime agreement by residues.

## The solve (step 5)
Full system (orders -9..-1, target_-5 = -(7/5) c_Gamma): inconsistent at (Gamma, s^-5) for all 7 graphs with the residuals listed above; (a) edge graphs: same for graphs 2..7; (b) s^-5 only: same. Minimal obstructed set = {(Gamma, s^-5)}; no other (graph, order) pair is obstructed.

Subleading system (s^-6 = s^-1 = s^-2 = 0 for all 7 graphs): consistent (contains M = 1). Z/5 covariance (colour shift with z -> zeta^-1 z) forces c_{shift mu} = zeta^{w} c_mu, so in Fourier modes L_{d,a} = Sum_i zeta^{a i} m1_{i,i+d} (d = 0,1,2) and B_{d,a} = Sum_i zeta^{a i} m2_{i,i+d} (d = 1,2):
- the 14 weight-1 equations span exactly the 3 modes L_{0,1}, L_{1,1}, L_{2,1} (rank 3): K = {L_{d,1} = 0}, dim 12. The s^-6 forms are c_{00} L_{0,1} + c_{01} L_{1,1} + c_{02} L_{2,1} with e.g. graph 1: (37/51200, z^3/25600, z/25600), graph 2: (-343/64000, -z^3/3200, -z/3200); the diagonal coefficients reproduce the SCALAR_SCAN column T1_-6 (c_{ii} = zeta^i T1_-6). The covariant scalar direction m1 = diag(a1 zeta^-i) has L_{0,1} = 5 a1 and is NOT in K (consistent with the scalar scan's a1 = 0).
- the m2 parts of the 7 s^-2 coefficients are all proportional to one form b = B_{1,2} + kappa B_{2,2} (rank 1; zero for graphs 3, 6, 7); its kernel is 9-dimensional (RREF basis in Q(zeta) in the log).
- the m1 m1 parts involve only products L_{d,a} L_{d',a'} with a + a' = 2 mod 5; on K: Q^Gamma = x^T C^Gamma y + z^T E^Gamma w with x = L_{.,0}, y = L_{.,2}, z = L_{.,3}, w = L_{.,4} (3x3 matrices logged). Eliminating b(m2) with graph 1 leaves 5 independent quadrics on K (graph 7's follows from Sum_Gamma = 0). Their common zero locus contains the four 6-dimensional linear subspaces {x = 0 or y = 0} x {z = 0 or w = 0} and is smooth of dimension 7 at random points of them (Jacobian rank 5 at both primes).
Solution set of the subleading system: {m1 in K on the 7-dimensional quadric locus} x {m2 : b(m2) = -Q^1(m1)/beta^1} (9-dimensional affine) x {m3 free}: dimension 16 in (m1, m2). Sample family: m1 with only the Fourier modes a in {2, 4} (x = z = 0, i.e. m1_{i,i+d} = (1/5)(zeta^{-2i} y_d + zeta^{-4i} w_d), 6 parameters) and any m2 with B_{1,2}(m2) + kappa B_{2,2}(m2) = 0: every such M keeps every stable graph's polar part equal to the point-frame one, c_Gamma t_c^-2 + c'_Gamma t_c^-1.

## Caveats
- Genus 2 only; constant M only (the task's choice). At genus >= 3 weight-5 monomials (m1^5, m2 m3, ...) reach the u-series orders, and q-dependent M is outside this scan.
- The dimension 7 of the quadric locus is a local statement at random points of the four linear subspaces (Jacobian rank), exact over F_p at both primes; the global geometry of the locus was not computed. kappa and the C, E matrices are Q(zeta) elements with several terms (logged as F_p residues; the equivalent data in the original variables are logged in Q(zeta)).
- fq_fp.ratrec at 2^61-1 cannot reconstruct denominators like 15360000; those entries print as residues at the second prime and are compared by residues in block (6). AI-checked only.
- Not a bug but noted: fq_graphs.Decorated's hodge_poly_nonzero pruning must not be used for colour-mixing vertex CohFTs (M.omega has non-zero genus-0 corrections); fq_msum enumerates its own decorations.
flags: The target (zero 1/t_c coefficient per stable graph) is unreachable for every graph by any constant symplectic factorisation, colour-mixing or not: the s^-5 coefficient is a weight-0 (M-independent) quantity by the mod-5 class bookkeeping, now verified numerically (random full M, and the fitted polynomials are constant at s^-10 and s^-5).

The subleading non-u-series coefficients (s^-6, s^-1, s^-2) can only be kept at their point-frame value zero; the solution set is a 16-dimensional family (m1 on a 7-dim quadric locus inside the 12-dim kernel of the three Z/5 modes L_{d,1}, m2 on a 9-dim affine space), containing the four linear 6-dim subspaces of m1 described in the report.
Reaching the 1/t_c coefficient would need weight = 0 mod 5 (genus >= 3) or q-dependent M, both outside the user's constant choice.
A concurrent process (genus2_diag.py by another session) was running in the same folder during this work; its log was not used.

minor: Flag/caveat 'Reaching the 1/t_c coefficient would need weight = 0 mod 5 (genus >= 3)' is imprecise: the weight-w part of every colour-summed decoration lies in s^{-10(g-1)+4w} Q(zeta)[[u]] (each row coefficient Q_{a,n} is s^{val} times a power series in u, verified by the referee for n <= 4; psi_{0,n}/L has a single L-class 4n mod 5 for n <= 7 in rows_check.log), so a weight-5j monomial starts at s^{-10(g-1)+20j}: at genus 3 weight 5 reaches only the constant term s^0, and a POLAR u-series coefficient (t_c^{-2}) first becomes reachable at genus 4. Suggested wording: 'genus >= 4 for a polar coefficient (genus 3: only the constant term)'. Same bookkeeping shows the stronger genus-2 statement, not made in the report: every u-series coefficient of every colour-summed graph, including the constant term s^0, is invariant under all constant symplectic M (consistent with pergraph_polar_out.txt, where F0, F1, F4, F5 share the s^0 coefficient graph by graph).

'Solution set ... dimension 16' (summary and flags) is a LOCAL dimension (Jacobian rank 5 at random points of the four 6-dimensional linear subspaces, reproduced exactly over Q(zeta) by the referee); the caveat says so, but the summary/flags state it flatly and 'described exactly by Z/5 Fourier modes' overstates: the quadric locus is given implicitly by 5 independent quadrics, its global geometry (other components, possibly of larger dimension) was not computed.

fq_sser.py docstring: 'the worst factor has nominal valuation +3: Q_{2,0}' -- val Q_{2,0} = +2 (it is P_{2,0} that has +3); the precision bound O(s^(prec_abs - 12)) that the Ser class actually tracks (log: total prec O(s^12) at prec_abs = 24) is correct, only the comment is off by one.

The fit's monomial basis (1, m1, m2, m3, m1 m1; 161) omits the weight-3 monomials m1^3 and m1 m2; their absence at polar orders is implied by the class argument and confirmed by the 9 surplus rows + 10 verification points, but the report should say so explicitly rather than only 'm3 never'.

The vertex CohFT M.omega for a genuinely colour-mixing M is validated only by (i) string/dilaton equations, (ii) the random-full-M total invariance, and (iii) the fit's polynomial structure; the N-ring cross-checks (phi_frame, diag_frame) are diagonal only. The referee's independent recomputation of graphs 1 and 4 at weight 1 (below) now covers the colour-mixing leg, kappa-leaf and inner-edge terms of M.omega at genus 1 and 2 for those two graphs; graphs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and all weight-2 (m2, off-diagonal m1 m1) coefficients rest on the project's own validation.

Weight bookkeeping Sum M-orders = 3g-3+n-Sum d re-derived; legged_graphs/automorphism filter, stability, connectivity and wtot check read and found consistent.

(2) Valuation bookkeeping with colour mixing: referee's own rows (built from the logged psi_{0,n}/L, the flat-basis recursion X_{a+1} = (zD + zeta^i L)X_a/(C1 kappa_a) with Cf(C1) = D t_c, and Z/5 covariance) reproduce the valuation table val Q_{a,n} = -4n + (0,-1,3,2,1)_a - 1 for all (a,n), n <= 4, colour independent, are symplectic for all 25 colour pairs to z^3, and each Q^{(0)}_{a,n} is s^{val} times a power series in u (single exponent class). (3) Independent recomputation (fresh Q(zeta) code, no project imports; scratch C:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d7c1b608d03d194a/37f24460-3601-4c85-b123-5156e19eb475/scratchpad/quintic_symp/referee/{ref_qz,ref_periods,ref_rows,ref_graph4,ref_graph1,ref_solve}.py): conifold Frobenius solutions f0 = 1 + (2/625)u^3, f1 = u - (19/60)u^3, f2 = u^2 + (37/30)u^3, gamma = 7/10, alpha = 0, t_c = u + (7/10)u^2 + (41/75)u^3 + (9/20)u^4 all re-derived from the standard quintic PF operator.
